binders: Two functions X, Y : Omega -> Real.
hypotheses: X belongs to L2(mu): it is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and has finite extended L2 seminorm.
Y belongs to L2(mu): it is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and has finite extended L2 seminorm.
conclusions: The absolute value of integral X(omega)Y(omega) dmu(omega) is at most norm(X,2)norm(Y,2), where each displayed L2 seminorm is obtained by converting the corresponding finite ENNReal-valued eLpNorm to a real number.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 mu f = integral f dmu.
MemLp f 2 mu means that f is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and eLpNorm f 2 mu is finite.
The norm of a real number is its absolute value.
The pointwise product is omega maps to X(omega)Y(omega).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any measure space and any two real-valued L2 functions X and Y, the absolute value of the integral of their pointwise product is bounded above by the product of their L2 seminorms.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: No probability, finiteness, sigma-finiteness, or nonzero assumption is imposed on mu; the statement is over an arbitrary measure.
The hypotheses use MemLp, so functions are considered through almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite extended L2 seminorm rather than requiring pointwise measurability everywhere.
ENNReal.toReal sends an infinite extended value to a finite real conventionally, but the MemLp hypotheses exclude infinity for both displayed L2 seminorms.

The Bochner integral has library-defined behavior even for non-integrable functions; here the two L2 hypotheses are intended to ensure that the product is integrable, although product integrability is not a separate explicit hypothesis.
The left side is the absolute value of a scalar integral, not the integral of the pointwise absolute value.
The result is a seminorm statement, so functions differing only on a mu-null set are not distinguished by the right-hand side.
ambiguities: The notation represented by eLpNorm is an extended Lp seminorm rather than a quotient-space norm, though finiteness under MemLp permits the usual real-valued L2 interpretation.
No explicit convention for writing the integral is present in the target beyond LocalDef001; its supplied definition resolves it as the Bochner integral with respect to mu.
